A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Efficient Network Automatic Relevance Determination with the same authors. All 22 pages, including Appendices A-F, are available and readable; text and visual inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments, timing comparisons, and biological, air-quality and stock-data analyses in Section 6 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results, including performance tables, timing measurements and inferred biological networks.

M1.justification: NARD, Sequential NARD, Surrogate NARD and Hybrid NARD retain the same objectives, update procedures and components. The kernel extension is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic data, aging cohort, seven TCGA cancer types, air-quality data and A-shares stocks. Appendix F adds no new coverage in v2.

E2.justification: MRCE, CAPME, HS-GHS and JRNS retain their experiment-specific participation in the comparisons. The newly cited graphical-lasso papers are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The five-fold parameter-selection procedure, synthetic dimensions and sparsity settings, TPR/FPR/Jaccard metrics, cancer sample sizes and stock-prediction window remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The scalability comparisons, polynomial/RBF kernel experiment and biological-network case studies are retained without revisions. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments are run ten times with different random seeds and averages are reported. No uncertainty-reporting or statistical-estimation practice changes.

E6.justification: The main-text and appendix results retain the same numerical values and qualitative findings. For example, Table 1 keeps NARD's TPR/FPR at 0.9483/0.0062 and Hybrid NARD's at 0.9471/0.0068.

T1.justification: The theorem, lemmas, propositions and derivations in the main text and Appendices A-D are unchanged mathematically. Equation-reference formatting and equivalent index placement do not revise the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: joint sparse regression and precision estimation, three computationally cheaper variants, comparable performance and applicability through kernel extensions.

C2.justification: The biological and stock-network interpretations remain unchanged. Appendix F.5 retains the same explanation of Surrogate NARD's numerical instability and suggestion of more robust precision-matrix initialization.

D1.justification: Hardware information, preprocessing descriptions, kernel choices and software/data access information are retained. No implementation or reproducibility information is substantively added or revised.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 and the bibliography add Banerjee et al. (2008) and Yuan and Lin (2007) to the graphical-lasso attribution. The broader research positioning, including Appendix E's Min-Min SBL discussion, is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 changes 'As shown in 3' to 'As shown in Table 3', standardizes Appendix B's equation references, edits a transition in Appendix D.2 and adjusts bibliographic capitalization. The narrative and section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Equation delimiter sizes and spacing change, notably around Equations (4) and (6), with local text and bibliography reflow. Figures 1-10 and Tables 1-8 retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: The added graphical-lasso references improve attribution, while clearer table and equation cross-references modestly improve navigation. Scientific content and evidence are unchanged. A new 'Atatistics' typo in Fan et al.'s journal title is a small editorial regression, but the overall gain remains slightly positive.
